title: Approve os_mem_alloc_aligned over-allocation alignment repair
summary: The target TODO cannot be retired against the frozen unix_mmapx executable path using only internal proof/spec propagation; unix_mmapx can return a successful mmap pointer with only page-alignment guarantees while callers require alignment up to SEGMENT_SIZE.
rationale: A proof-only attempt added internal alignment postconditions through os_mem_alloc/unix_mmap/unix_mmapx while restoring the frozen unix_mmapx body. Verification failed at both successful unix_mmapx return exits because the sanctioned mmap wrapper contracts do not imply requested-alignment or hint-equality. The concrete os_alloc.rs patch over-allocates by try_alignment and splits the mapped MemChunk to an aligned subrange, which establishes the existing os_mem_alloc_aligned postcondition without changing frozen goal contracts or os_mem.rs.
machine_evidence: Attempt pa-1 first failing VC: os_alloc.rs:321:13 postcondition not satisfied at unix_mmapx returns on lines 350 and 360. With the over-allocation candidate applied, make verify exits 0 with 738 verified/0 errors, boundary_guard and spec_drift pass, proof_state next no longer lists os_mem_alloc_aligned as a direct types.rs::todo caller, literal non-lib todo count is 11, and ast_consistency remains red with 4 mismatches due frozen-exec changes requiring review.
first_failing_vc: os_alloc.rs:321:13 postcondition not satisfied at unix_mmapx successful return exits when proving try_alignment > 1 ==> addr % try_alignment == 0 on the frozen executable path
implementation_inventory: verus-mimalloc/os_alloc.rs::os_mem_alloc_aligned removes the target todo branch and relies on propagated alignment
verus-mimalloc/os_alloc.rs::os_mem_alloc and ::unix_mmap propagate an internal alignment postcondition
verus-mimalloc/os_alloc.rs::unix_mmapx over-allocates for try_alignment > 1, aligns inside the mapping, and splits MemChunk to the returned range
established_facts: The frozen unix_mmapx body returns successful mmap_prot_read_write/mmap_prot_none results directly after an optional hint attempt.
The sanctioned os_mem.rs wrappers do not expose a contract that a successful mmap result equals a nonzero hint or is aligned above page_size.
The applied os_alloc.rs over-allocation patch is the concrete middle-layer behavior change that proves the target postcondition without modifying os_mem.rs or frozen goal contracts.
residual_uncertainty: Operator/reviewer must decide whether this frozen-executable change is acceptable, or whether a separate external mmap contract decision should be made instead.

options.label: overallocate-and-split
options.trade: Changes os_alloc.rs executable behavior for try_alignment > 1; avoids strengthening os_mem.rs and proves the returned MemChunk covers the aligned subrange.

review_reason: Candidate od-1 is semantically earned and now requires operator authority. I independently reran the relevant gates: `make verify` exits 0 with `738 verified, 0 errors`; `boundary_guard` passes with no net TCB growth and frozen goal contracts byte-identical; `spec_drift` is clean for `verus-mimalloc/os_alloc.rs`; refreshed `proof_state next` reports `os_mem_alloc_aligned@L136` as `in_verification` with no `types.rs::todo@L2210` trust leaf, and the remaining `types.rs::todo` callers are other sites; the non-lib literal `todo();` count is 11. The blockers are exactly the reviewed escalation state: `ast_consistency` remains red with 4 mismatches, and `operator_decisions gate` reports `CANDIDATE_REVIEW` for od-1. Attempt pa-1 records the proof-only frozen-path failure at `os_alloc.rs:321:13`: the frozen `unix_mmapx` can return a successful mmap result directly, while the sanctioned `os_mem.rs` mmap contracts do not guarantee requested alignment or hint equality. Strengthening that bottom boundary is disallowed by this mission, so the currently verified repair depends on an executable over-allocation-and-split change in `os_alloc.rs`, which cannot be accepted silently.
operator_question: Approve od-1: allow the verified `os_alloc.rs` frozen-exec over-allocation-and-split repair in `unix_mmapx` to retire the `os_mem_alloc_aligned` alignment TODO without strengthening `os_mem.rs`?
resolution_note:
REJECTED. The diagnosis in pa-1 is accepted as correct: the sanctioned os_mem.rs mmap contracts guarantee only page alignment, so the os_mem_alloc_aligned postcondition cannot be discharged by internal proof/spec propagation alone. The over-allocation SHAPE is also the right idea. The submitted patch is rejected for three concrete defects, not for its direction.

(1) WRONG PLACEMENT. The patch installs the over-allocation at the top of unix_mmapx and takes it unconditionally whenever try_alignment > 1. The todo() being retired lives in os_mem_alloc_aligned, on the FALLBACK path that is reached only after os_mem_alloc has already returned a pointer and that pointer turned out to be misaligned (p.addr() % alignment != 0). A rare fallback has been turned into the always-taken path: every segment allocation now maps SEGMENT_ALIGN (32 MiB) of extra address space, not just the misaligned ones. Fix the site where the todo() actually is, and only on the misalignment branch.

(2) THE RECLAIM IS FICTIONAL. MemChunk::split is a proof fn (os_mem_util.rs:34). It is pure ghost: it partitions the permission token and has no effect whatsoever on the operating system. After the split the patch returns aligned_mem and drops the remainder, so the head padding and the tail surplus remain mapped in the process address space forever while their permission is discarded and can never be recovered. Splitting a ghost permission is not releasing memory. Whatever you over-allocate, you must actually give back.

(3) BYPASSES THE EXISTING ALIGNMENT MECHANISM. The new branch returns before the hint logic, so os_get_aligned_hint never runs when try_alignment > 1. That path exists precisely to obtain an aligned address on the first attempt. Do not delete a working mechanism and replace it with an unconditional worst case; the fallback must sit behind it, not in front of it.

Standing constraints are unchanged: no net-new trust, no weakening or strengthening of a sanctioned contract to assume a property the underlying syscall does not actually provide, no ensures false, and no substituting one escape hatch for another. Record the outcome of this review and any further failed approaches in research/proof_attempts.jsonl. If after that you conclude that no correct implementation of this fallback is expressible with the operations currently available to the project, say so explicitly in a new candidate, name the exact missing capability and why project code cannot provide it, and let the operator decide.
